06001.page_note: Under a county agreement running 7/1/2025 to 6/30/2031, with a five-year service period starting 7/1/2026, AMR West holds the emergency ambulance area covering all cities and unincorporated areas except Alameda, Albany, Berkeley, Piedmont and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. The fire departments of Alameda, Albany, Berkeley and Piedmont run their own emergency ambulance areas, and the laboratory is served by Alameda County Fire. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the state EMS authority's January 2026 list still names Falck, and no source dated after the July 1, 2026 start confirms the change.

06065.page_note: The state EMS authority's January 2026 list names AMR (7 zones), Riverside County Fire/CAL FIRE (Cove Cities, Indio), Cathedral City Fire, Idyllwild Fire Protection District and Blythe Ambulance. AMR's contract was set to expire June 30, 2026, and extensions were denied (Idyllwild Town Crier, Nov 2023). Not yet confirmed from a public source: who provides service after July 2026.

06077.page_note: CENCAL Fire and EMS Authority holds the exclusive emergency ambulance contract for Zones X and Y, May 1, 2026 to May 1, 2031 (county Board of Supervisors, Feb 10, 2026). Other zones per the state EMS authority's January 2026 list: Manteca District Ambulance (Zone D), Ripon Fire Protection District (E) and Escalon Community Ambulance (F). Not yet confirmed from a public source: Zone Y boundaries and any other zones; the state list still shows AMR for Zone X (Lodi).

06095.page_note: The state EMS authority's January 2026 list names Medic Ambulance for the county except the Vacaville area, and Vacaville Fire Department for Vacaville and the surrounding unincorporated area. The contract is on short extensions, and a new request for proposals with a Fairfield/Medic joint bid is in progress (Daily Republic). Not yet confirmed from a public source: the award, and who serves Travis Air Force Base.

06037.page_note: AMR serves the county's Area 1; Care Ambulance serves Areas 2-5; McCormick Ambulance serves Areas 6-9, per the state EMS authority's January 2026 list of 34 zones. About 24 city fire departments, including Los Angeles (also San Fernando), Long Beach, Glendale, Pasadena, Santa Monica and Torrance, run their own ambulances. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the county EMS agency's own list of providers.

06073.page_note: The state EMS authority's January 2026 list names providers for 30 of the county's 31 areas: Falck for the City of San Diego; AMR for CSA-17, El Cajon, Grossmont and National City; San Diego County Fire Protection District for the inland areas; the fire departments of Carlsbad, Chula Vista, Coronado, Escondido, Oceanside, Poway, San Marcos, Vista and Santee/Lakeside; North County Fire Protection District; and tribal and Department of Defense areas. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the Harmony Grove Service Area, listed only as 'closest available resource', and the county EMS agency's own list.

06059.page_note: The state EMS authority's January 2026 list names Orange County Fire Authority Regions A-E (Emergency Ambulance Service, Care) and city ambulance areas served by Care, Huntington Beach Fire, Newport Beach Fire, Orange Fire, La Habra, Doctor's Ambulance (Laguna Beach) and San Clemente city/Orange County Fire Authority. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the county EMS agency's own list, or any city changes since 2024.

06071.page_note: The state EMS authority's January 2026 list shows 26 areas. The Unified Area (exclusive areas 1-4) is marked 'HOLD until contract received', and area 26 (Havasu Lake) shows 'No approved provider'. Not yet confirmed from a public source: who serves those areas.

06085.page_note: The state EMS authority's January 2026 list names Rural/Metro of California (AMR) for the county except Palo Alto (non-exclusive), and Palo Alto Fire Department. A county request for proposals for a new exclusive ambulance contract was in draft in July 2026. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the county EMS agency's own list.

06067.page_note: The state EMS authority's January 2026 list shows one non-exclusive county zone whose licensees (including Alpha One, AMR, Bay Medic, CHP and CALSTAR) are not 911 transporters. Not yet confirmed from a public source: the fire departments that provide 911 transport (Sacramento Fire, Sacramento Metro Fire, Cosumnes, Folsom and others), which need a Sacramento County EMS source.
